newsitem.title: USA: Rouge Steel boosts production, Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: Rouge Steel boosts production, Q1 net.

text.p: Rouge Steel Co said Tuesday that improved production from its blast furnaces and a bigger share of the automotive sheet steel market allowed it to boost first quarter earnings by 39 percent over a year earlier.
Rouge Steel, which operates a single integrated mill here, reported first quarter net income rose to $9.3 million from $6.7 million a year earlier.
It said steel product shipments in the first quarter totaled 744,000 tons, up 42,000 tons or six percent from a year ago, reflecting record shipments to the automotive sector.

Raw steel production totaled 748,000 tons, an an increase of 94,000 tons over the first quarter of 1996 and up 228,000 tons from the 1996 fourth quarter, when production was hurt by relining work on the company's biggest blast furnace.
"We are pleased with the steady increase in blast furnace production since the reline of our largest blast furnace in the fourth quarter of 1996," Rouge Chairman Carl Valdiserri said in a statement.

"Our production trend is on target with our plan to balance and fully utilize our manufacturing facilities and to meet the increased demand of our customers with a lower requirement for purchased slabs," he added.

Valdiserri said the company plans to upgrade its primary steel production facilities in the fourth quarter of 1997, and improve its hot strip mill and tandem mill as part of an effort to reduce costs, improve quality and enhance product offerings.
"Our order book continues to be strong through the second quarter and we expect 1997 to be a good year," Valdiserri said.
